name: Water rinse after coffee
lead: Rinsing the mouth with plain water after drinking coffee is a habit discussed in tooth-whitening and appearance communities as a way to reduce stain build-up.

Dental references describe coffee and tea tannins as chromogens that can stain teeth with frequent intake, and say that most extrinsic stain is removable by cleaning.[2][3] Plaque and calculus can also hold stain.[3]
No studies of water rinsing and staining were found.

paras: Practitioners rinse or swallow water after coffee. Some also brush afterward, though no source reviewed addresses timing. Plaque stained by chromogenic bacteria and neglected calculus are among surface stain sources in dental references.[3]

Extrinsic stains from coffee are on the surface, and treatments include whitening toothpaste or professional scaling and polishing.[3] Whitening by toothpaste is by abrasion of surface stain.[1] Frequent acidic drinks are a recognised cause of erosion, per tooth wear literature.[4] Whether water rinsing changes staining or erosion has not been tested in the sources reviewed.

card.summary: Swishing water after coffee to cut stain build-up; harmless habit with no stain data.
card.note: No studies of rinsing and staining found.

quick.overview:
This means rinsing with water after coffee so pigments do not linger on the teeth.

Dental sources describe coffee as a cause of extrinsic stain but report no studies of water rinsing.
quick.mechanism: Water is meant to wash residual pigment from tooth surfaces before it binds.
quick.risks: No harms are documented; benefit is untested.
